title: Pulled Pork Sandwiches
shortDescription: Slow-smoked pull, soft buns, fast line
subtitle: Slow-smoked pull, soft buns, fast line
description: Sandwich line for the whole hall. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large covered roaster or slow cooker

steps.title: Apply dry rub
steps.instruction: Trim excess hard fat from pork shoulder, leaving about ¼ inch. Mix brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Coat pork all over and press rub into the surface. Rest at room temp 30 minutes while the oven or slow cooker comes up.

steps.title: Low-and-slow cook
steps.instruction: Roast at 275°F in a covered roaster or run a slow cooker on low 8–10 hours until pork probes tender at 203°F and shreds with a fork. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry halfway through — you want steam, not a dry roast.

steps.title: Rest and shred
steps.instruction: Rest pork covered 30 minutes — juices redistribute. Shred with two forks, discarding large fat chunks. Toss with apple cider vinegar first, then fold in BBQ sauce to taste. Keep some sauce on the side for the line.

steps.title: Quick slaw
steps.instruction: Toss coleslaw mix with mayonnaise, a splash of vinegar, salt, and pepper. Keep cold until service — hot pork plus cold slaw is the move.

steps.title: Warm buns for the line
steps.instruction: Split brioche or kaiser rolls and warm wrapped in foil at 300°F for 5 minutes until soft and steamy. Stack cut-side up on sheet trays — cold buns kill BBQ sandwich morale.

steps.title: Stage the sandwich counter
steps.instruction: Set shredded pork in a deep hotel pan with a ladle of cooking juices on top. Line buns, slaw, pickles, and extra BBQ sauce in separate bowls with tongs. Hot pork center, cold crunch at the far end.

steps.title: Build pulled pork sandwiches
steps.instruction: Crew piles pork on buns and tops with slaw and pickles. This is BBQ pulled pork — soft buns and tangy slaw, not Italian subs. Keep extra sauce on the line for crews who want more smoke.

steps.title: Verify pork hold temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the pork pan — service temp should stay at or above 140°F. If below, return to a 200°F oven covered until steaming. Shredded pork that reads under 140°F gets reheated to 165°F before the line reopens.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover shredded pork — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool shredded pork and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Pull pork at 203°F when it shreds with a fork — rushing the roast gives tough sandwiches.
Toss with vinegar before BBQ sauce so the pull tastes bright, not one-note sweet.
Keep slaw cold on ice — hot pork plus cold slaw is the hall move.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Condiments: pickle chips, extra BBQ sauce, yellow mustard
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool shredded pork in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Reheat pork with a splash of apple cider vinegar and broth so it stays saucy, not dry.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Slow-smoked pull, soft buns, fast line. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
